findings.title: `website_name` is missing `?` on its `include_` method and is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`
findings.body: `UserSerializer` defines `def include_website_name` without a trailing question mark (ActiveModel::Serializer requires `include_website_name?`), and does not include `:website_name` in the `untrusted_attributes` list on line 105 (which already includes `:website`). Because `include_website_name?` is never defined, AMS always serializes `website_name`—even as `nil` when a user has no website, and even for TL0 users viewed by anonymous visitors when `restrict_user_fields?` is true, leaking the user's website domain/path despite `website` itself being suppressed (`user.hbs` renders `{{model.website_name}}` whenever it is truthy). Adding `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (and removing the broken `include_website_name` method) fixes both issues.

findings.title: Saving user preferences does not update `website_name` on the client model
findings.body: Previously `websiteName` was a computed property on the user controller observing `model.website`, so editing and saving the `website` field in user preferences immediately updated the displayed website name on the profile page without a reload. Now `website_name` is computed server-side in `UserSerializer`, but `User#save` (around line 210 of `user.js.es6`) only copies `bio_excerpt` from the `PUT /users/:username` response back onto the model (`self.set('bio_excerpt', data.user.bio_excerpt)`). After a user updates their `website` in preferences and navigates back to their profile, `model.website_name` remains stale (or undefined if they had no website before) until a full page refresh.
